source.title: Kernel Normalized Convolutional Networks
source.authors: Reza Nasirigerdeh; Reihaneh Torkzadehmahani; D. Rueckert; Georgios Kaissis

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch normalization claims in new normalization-layer settings, reporting convergence and accuracy comparisons for kernel-normalized networks across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet and other tasks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own normalization comparisons and convergence claims, which bear on V6. Test-accuracy values do not measure training classification error or the V1–V5 outcomes. The CIFAR-10 loss-landscape result measures generalization and curvature, not those versions. Cited prior-work claims were not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its proposed KernelNorm method against other normalization methods. It does not test adding BatchNorm against the same network without normalization, learning-rate tolerance, or the Fixup recipe. Faster convergence with KernelNorm than BatchNorm does not contradict V6, which does not claim BatchNorm is faster than every alternative.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that KNResNets achieve higher or competitive predictive performance against BatchNorm counterparts, outperform the tested batch-independent competitors, and converge faster in the displayed case studies. Faster convergence refers to epochs; the implementation takes longer per epoch than BatchNorm.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces KernelNorm and KNConv as alternative batch-independent normalization layers and compares their resulting networks with BatchNorm, LayerNorm and GroupNorm models; it does not test the original BatchNorm intervention directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported comparisons vary with dataset, architecture, batch size, and metric; KNResNet-50 at CIFAR-100 batch size 32 and pixel accuracy on CityScapes for KNResNet-18/34 are slightly below BatchNorm.

fits_no_version.finding: KernelNorm models generally match or exceed BatchNorm models in final classification and segmentation performance; several individual metrics are slightly lower.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KernelNorm architectures can achieve competitive predictive performance against BatchNorm architectures across the tested datasets and batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: KernelNorm achieves 22.01% DP classification accuracy, versus 20.81% with LayerNorm and 20.99% with GroupNorm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KernelNorm improves predictive accuracy over LayerNorm and GroupNorm in the tested DP-SGD setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report faster convergence per epoch for KernelNorm in Figure 4's four case studies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KernelNorm architectures converge faster per epoch than the evaluated normalization competitors in these settings.

record.problems: The reported performance outcomes are primarily test accuracy and segmentation metrics, not training-error measurements. Convergence comparisons are described in text and Figure 4 without exact numeric convergence values; ImageNet Table 2 reports no uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported results were left out. Results comparing LayerNorm/GroupNorm/LocalContextNorm only with each other, DP BatchNorm marked NA, the ConvNext comparison, CIFAR-10 test accuracy/loss landscape, and the KernelNorm/dropout ablation do not directly measure the V6 normalization comparison as phrased or the V1–V5 outcomes.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random labels, and its dependence on size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training degradation in plain networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery, divergence, and sharpness dynamics relative to the learning-rate stability threshold.
Training acceleration and higher learning-rate tolerance from adding BatchNorm to the same network; equally fast and stable training using Fixup without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted V6 verdicts. Neither competitive final accuracy nor KernelNorm's occasional deficits establish support or scope limits for V6. Table 5 reports accuracy-selected learning rates, not maximum stable learning rates. The KernelNorm ablation and CIFAR-10 loss-landscape analysis also do not test the stated versions.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model width, and CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 train error are not reported.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minima rate, or student-width comparison.
No comparison of plain and identity-shortcut networks for training error or depth-related degradation.
No initialization comparison or measurement of signal propagation, gradient flow, or trainable depth.
No learning-rate-above-stability experiment or curvature-threshold measurement.

Tests KernelNorm against BatchNorm and batch-independent normalization competitors, including convergence speed. Does not compare the same network with and without BatchNorm across every version’s specified datasets and architectures; does not report learning-rate tolerance comparisons.

relation.reason: Uses normalization's optimization benefits to motivate and evaluate its proposed method; does not compare adding BatchNorm with the same network without normalization or evaluate Fixup.

tranche.reason: Evaluates KernelNorm against existing normalization methods without testing a claim version's specified intervention or recipe.

source_check.notes: Convergence comparisons concern epochs, not elapsed training time; Appendix D reports longer training time per epoch for KernelNorm. CityScapes baselines use SyncBatchNorm; differential privacy comparisons exclude BatchNorm.
